body:
maya: quick sync — we need a firm contract for the runtime -> telemetry pipeline so console can show slot visibility and queue-tail behavior for Hosted + Dedicated pools

jesse: agree. what's the minimum fields you need?

rachel: owners: console needs: pool_id, pool_type (hosted|dedicated), model_family, sm_id, sm_occupancy_pct, sm_alloc_bytes, queue_depth, queue_tail_latency_ms, sample_ts

dan: for infra: also include host_region, instance_type, and a signal for whether SM is preemptible. we need labels for routing policies later.

alex: sampling cadence question — if runtime emits per-sm every 5s that's heavy. can we emit aggregated rollups per-pool every 10s and detailed per-sm every 60s?

jesse: runtime proposal: default rollup 10s, detailed 60s. include `sample_type` label: `rollup` or `detailed`. can switch per-customer via config.

maya: that works. console will use `rollup` for heatmaps and `detailed` when you click into a pool. UX note: avoid gaps when switching rollouts — console should interpolate short gaps <15s.

rachel: for dashboards we want these metric names (Prom metric style):
```
redwood_sm_occupancy_percent{pool_id, pool_type, model_family, sm_id, sample_type}
redwood_sm_alloc_bytes{...}
redwood_sm_queue_depth{...}
redwood_sm_queue_tail_latency_ms{...}
```

jesse: sending a sample event now to test ingest (will include host_region + instance_type).

deploy-bot: ingest: metric packet accepted (id=f2c9). latency=120ms.

dan: excellent — two infra constraints: 1) for Dedicated, metrics may come from customer VPC exporter (pull model) so we need a consistent label mapping; 2) add `source=runtime|vpc_exporter` label

alex: edge case: quantized models reduce mem footprints drastically — `sm_alloc_bytes` should be nullable or zero when not applicable, and we should track `quantization_profile` label.

maya: good catch. include `quant_profile` label optional. console will hide alloc when zero.

rachel: alerting: propose baseline SLOs on queue_tail_latency_ms p50/p95 per-pool and an occupancy spike alert when sm_occupancy_percent > 95% for >2m. owners: eng-platform + eng-oncall.

jesse: implementation note: runtime currently reports `sm_util` (0-1). i'll add translation to percent and the new names. patch incoming.

maya: ownership: runtime (jesse) owns emit, eng-infra (dan) owns ingestion + label canonicalization, console (rachel) owns dashboard shape + interpolator, eng-platform (maya) owns rollout UX and quota mapping.

dan: can we add a small JSON schema for ingestion so exporter teams can validate? something like:
```
{
  "metric": "redwood_sm_occupancy_percent",
  "labels": ["pool_id","pool_type","sm_id","sample_type","source","host_region"],
  "value": 73.2,
  "ts": 1732104321000
}
```

rachel: yes please — console will reject unknown labels. also please add `model_variant` optional label for dedicated customers who pin versions.

alex: rollout plan: canary emit for 24h on a subset of hosted pools, then enable for Dedicated (non-customer-facing) for a week, then GA. we should have a revert toggle if ingest cost > threshold.

maya: UX: add a toggle in Console -> Pools to choose rollup vs per-sm detail, and a notice when detailed sampling is rate-limited.

jesse: i'll open PR with: emitter + config flag + `sample_type` label. linking in a minute.

rachel: i'll stub dashboard tiles and wire alerts to eng-oncall.

dan: infra will add canonicalizer that maps `vpc_exporter` labels into our standard names. will post schema by EOD.

maya: thanks all. action items:
- jesse: PR for emitter + canary flag (due tomorrow)
- dan: canonicalizer + schema doc (EOD)
- rachel: dashboard stubs + alert rules (EOD)
- alex: cost threshold proposal for detailed sampling (EOD)

jesse: noted. starting PR now.

alex: will run simulated load to estimate ingest QPS and cost.

rachel: quick Q: metrics retention? console needs 90d for rollups, 14d for detailed. ok?

dan: infra can do 90/14 as a default tier. Dedicated customers can opt-in for longer retention as an add-on.

maya: perfect. i'll schedule a 30m follow-up tomorrow to review the schema and the first canary results. :thumbsup:
